Yajurveda.fact: The Upanishad is the legendary story of a little boy, Nachiketa – the son of sage Vajasravasa, who meets Yama – the Indian deity of death.

Yajurveda.subject: Sanskrit & Classical Languages
Yajurveda.question: Their conversation evolves to a discussion of the nature of man, knowledge, Ātman (_____, Self) and moksha (liberation)
Yajurveda.fact: I (Soul, Self) am the treasure, wise, immortal, imperishable. Their conversation evolves to a discussion of the nature of man, knowledge, Ātman (Soul, Self) and moksha (liberation).

Yajurveda.subject: Sanskrit & Classical Languages
Yajurveda.question: The Kathaka Upanishad is an important ancient _____ corpus of the Vedanta sub-schools
Yajurveda.fact: The Kathaka Upanishad is an important ancient Sanskrit corpus of the Vedanta sub-schools.

Yajurveda.subject: Sanskrit & Classical Languages
Yajurveda.question: It asserts that "Atman (Soul, Self) exists", teaches the precept "seek Self-knowledge which is _____", and expounds on this premise like the other primary Upanishads of Hinduism
Yajurveda.fact: It asserts that "Atman (Soul, Self) exists", teaches the precept "seek Self-knowledge which is Highest Bliss", and expounds on this premise like the other primary Upanishads of Hinduism.

Yajurveda.subject: Sanskrit & Classical Languages
Yajurveda.question: The detailed teachings of _____ have been variously interpreted, as Dvaita (dualistic) and as Advaita (non-dualistic)
Yajurveda.fact: The detailed teachings of Katha Upanishad have been variously interpreted, as Dvaita (dualistic) and as Advaita (non-dualistic). The Katha Upanishad found in the Yajurveda is among the most widely studied Upanishads.

Yajurveda.subject: Sanskrit & Classical Languages
Yajurveda.question: The Shvetashvatara Upanishad is notable for its discussion of the concept of personal god – _____, and suggesting it to be a path to one's own Highest Self
Yajurveda.fact: The Shvetashvatara Upanishad is notable for its discussion of the concept of personal god – Ishvara, and suggesting it to be a path to one's own Highest Self.

Yajurveda.subject: Sanskrit & Classical Languages
Yajurveda.question: The text is also notable for its multiple mentions of both _____ and Shiva, along with other Vedic deities, and of crystallization of Shiva as a central theme
Yajurveda.fact: The text is also notable for its multiple mentions of both Rudra and Shiva, along with other Vedic deities, and of crystallization of Shiva as a central theme.

Yajurveda.subject: Sanskrit & Classical Languages
Yajurveda.question: It consists of seven _____ (lessons)
Yajurveda.fact: It consists of seven Prapathakas (lessons). However, several manuscripts discovered in different parts of India contain lesser number of Prapathakas, with a Telugu-language version showing just four.

Yajurveda.question: The Maitrayaniya Upanishad is notable for its references to theories also found in _____, elements of the Samkhya and Yoga schools of Hinduism, as well as the Ashrama system
Yajurveda.fact: The Maitrayaniya Upanishad is notable for its references to theories also found in Buddhism, elements of the Samkhya and Yoga schools of Hinduism, as well as the Ashrama system.

Yajurveda.subject: Sanskrit & Classical Languages
Yajurveda.question: The Ezourveda was studied by _____, and later declared a forgery, representing Jesuit ideas to Indians as a Vedic school
